q: During surgery in the sitting position, EtCO2 falls suddenly, SpO2 drops and BP falls. What is the most likely diagnosis?
why: Open venous sinuses above the heart entrain air. Signs: falling EtCO2 and SpO2, arrhythmia, hypotension, rising right atrial pressure.

q: What is the first step in managing venous air embolism during posterior fossa surgery?
o: Tell the surgeon to flood the field with saline and stop further air entry
why: Prevent more air entering: flood the field and use wet packs, lower the head, stop N2O, FiO2 1.0, aspirate the CVC.

q: Which monitor is most sensitive for detecting venous air embolism?
why: TOE and precordial Doppler are the most sensitive.

q: Which is an absolute contraindication to the sitting position?
o: A right-to-left intracardiac shunt or ventriculo-atrial shunt
why: Right-to-left shunts risk paradoxical air embolism; a PFO is a relative contraindication.

q: During posterior fossa surgery the heart rate suddenly falls to 35 with hypertension. What is the likely cause?
why: Brainstem manipulation causes sudden bradycardia and BP changes; tell the surgeon to stop.

q: Why must swallow and airway reflexes be checked before extubation after posterior fossa surgery?
o: Lower cranial nerve (IX–XII) injury can cause bulbar dysfunction and aspiration
why: The posterior fossa contains cranial nerves VII–XII; injury causes dysphagia and impaired airway reflexes.

q: Why is post-operative vomiting common after posterior fossa surgery?
o: Surgery is close to the vomiting centre
why: Proximity to the vomiting centre (area postrema) increases PONV; give regular antiemetics.

q: What does the acronym DANISH describe?
why: Dysdiadochokinesia, ataxia, nystagmus, intention tremor, slurred speech, hypotonia.

q: A patient with an acoustic neuroma (vestibular schwannoma) has a reduced corneal reflex. Which nerve is affected?
why: The corneal reflex afferent is V; acoustic neuromas affect VIII, then V and VII as they grow.

q: Which complication of prolonged surgery in the sitting or prone position affects the airway after extubation?
why: Neck flexion and prolonged surgery cause tongue and airway oedema (macroglossia).
